cases.note: Recorded NORMAL business history with reconstruction after every batch: left join, grouping and revision replacement all agree when no support boundary is crossed.
One child feeds two union edges: shared subplan propagation keeps multiplicities exact through duplicate source rows.

NULL never equals NULL: null-key left rows stay padded and anti-kept, duplicate nulls never match, and a non-null key only flips when an equality actually holds. No padding boundary is crossed by a right change, so the outer-join retraction defect cannot mask the NULL semantics.
NULL grouping keys coalesce; a zero SUM with nonzero COUNT is a real group; all-NULL value rows feed COUNT(*) but leave SUM NULL.

Tombstone then later revision revives a record through the filter; an empty batch still advances generation with an empty delta. Receipt replay idempotency for a repeated batch id is asserted separately in checks.py (a replayed receipt carries the original generation and therefore cannot equal a zero net delta).
Recorded incident: right-side first match must retract the padded left row; the engine adds the matched group but never retracts the NULL extension.
Anti join ignores right deltas entirely: right-only insert/delete flips existence but the anti bag never changes, including after SQLite reconstruction.
Both join inputs change in one batch: the da x db cross pair is counted twice because both contributions use the new opposite bag.
DISTINCT flips on the sign of each delta instead of a maintained support count: support 2 -> 1 wrongly retracts the row.
HAVING-suppressed groups persist no accumulators: when the group becomes visible again SUM/COUNT restart from only the new delta.
The keyless global group must always exist as [null,0,0]; when the input empties the engine drops it instead of re-emitting it.

Reverse boundary of M1: deleting the last right match must re-add the all-NULL extension; only the matched pair is retracted. The matched baseline is built by inserting the left row after the right, so no earlier defect corrupts the state under test.

Combined-history defect distinct from M3: a changed left row whose right match disappears in the same batch is padded against the new bag, losing the old-occurrence padding flip. The matched baseline is established by left-after-right inserts so the final simultaneous batch is the only batch whose both sides change.
In a combined batch the changed-left existence test itself uses the correct new right bag, but the unchanged left occurrence's flip is still lost because db is ignored: isolates the two anti causes.

Shared DAG propagation around a join whose right edge is a DISTINCT node: single-side batches confirm correct propagation through the shared node, then the final both-side batch shows the new cross pair double counted because each contribution reads the new opposite bag.
